summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,652.86, down 0.28% for a second straight session, while the Dow finished at 53,417.16, up 0.26%, as the same rotation that dominated Monday continued: money leaving Technology, which fell 1.78%, and landing in Consumer Staples up 1.70%, Financials up 1.29%, and Utilities up 1.05%. The 10 year yield eased to 4.70%, down 0.72%, as Treasury Secretary Bessent signaled buybacks of more than 4 billion dollars and a possible tap of the Treasury General Account to push long yields lower, a move that lifted TLT to 82.56. Gold held at 4,691.40, up 1.09%, Bitcoin traded at 79,318.25, up 0.45%, and WTI crude fell hard to 82.20, down 3.31%, as US Iran sanctions came in softer than feared for trading partners and oil markets exhaled. The biggest single stock stories were concentrated in semiconductors and quantum computing: MU fell 5.83%, IONQ dropped 8.47%, WDC lost 5.24%, and NVDA declined 2.91% on above average volume, all in the 24 hours before NVIDIA reports earnings Wednesday. The Canada US trade war intensified further, with Ottawa announcing retaliatory tariffs and Trump threatening 50 percent levies on Canadian autos, a direct headwind for the Canadian portion of the book and for CM.TO and RY.TO both of which report Wednesday. The week's key events are still ahead: Core PCE and preliminary GDP Wednesday, unemployment claims Thursday, and Fed Chair Warsh speaking Friday.
